name: Cable Front Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that targets the anterior deltoid by raising a low cable attachment in front of the body under constant tension.

setup: Set the cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a straight bar or dual-handled rope.
Straddle the cable facing away from the machine, or stand facing it, gripping the handle with an overhand grip.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly soft, and arms extended downward with a slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Brace your core and raise the attachment forward in a controlled arc until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize contraction in the front of the shoulders.
Lower the attachment with control along the same path back to the starting position without letting the stack slam.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the cable forward; inhale as you lower it back down with control.
cues: Keep a soft bend in the elbows
Don't lean back to initiate the lift

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso and leaning back to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and keep your core braced to isolate movement entirely to the shoulder joint.

common_faults.fault: Raising the arms excessively high above eye level.
common_faults.correction: Stop when the arms are roughly parallel to the floor or shoulder height to keep tension on the anterior deltoid.
Maintain a fixed, slight bend in the elbows throughout the entire movement.

precautions: Avoid using excessive loads that force hyperextension of the lumbar spine.
